messages:
anika: Heads up, dashboards showing a quick 99p latency jump for text-gen in na1-edge, started ~5m ago. KV cache miss rate spiked from 2% -> 22%.
ryan: seeing it too. 99p tokens latency from 180ms -> 1.4s. console link: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/latency?region=na1
liam: any recent runtime/pack changes rolled to na1?
anika: there was a small batching tweak from PR#452 that tweaked continuous-batching thresholds, rolled 00:10 UTC.
jason: can we confirm it's batching vs an infra flake? Miss rate suggests KV cache churn.
maya: logs show a flood of cache evictions around the same time. Possibly eviction heuristics + batch change increased concurrency and fragmented caches.
ryan: routing note: na1 hotpool is at 92% GPU alloc, other pools have headroom. We can shift low-priority traffic to na2 to reduce pressure.
liam: steps: 1) throttle background/batchable routes 2) rollback PR#452 to canary 3) drain a couple of stressed hotpool nodes 4) warm KV cache on fallback nodes
anika: I'm throttling batchable route now (control-plane request).
ops-bot: Throttle request accepted: route=batchable-gen, rate=30r/s (effective). :white_check_mark:
ryan: initiating routing shift policy: route low-priority 20% -> eu-west (na->eu). Doing gradual 5% steps.
infra-bot: Evacuation started for pool na1-hotpool-7: draining 2 GPUs. Command: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-na1-7 && kubectl drain node/gpu-na1-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
maya: I'm pushing rollback to canary 1. Rolling back PR#452 commit 9d4b2c to previous.
ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-service rollout/rollback to tag v1.12.3-rc -> v1.12.2 (canary).
jason: while rollback goes, can we reduce batch max_tokens to 64 on na1 to reduce in-flight KV sizes? Small change, hotfixable via config.
liam: Good call. Pushing config change to na1 edge config: `EDGE_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=64`
anika: applied batch size cap. Monitoring.
ryan: after config change 1m: 99p dropped 1.4s -> 820ms, KV miss still high (~15%).
maya: can we prewarm caches on nodes we are shifting traffic to? There's an endpoint to prepopulate popular prefixes.
ops-bot: Prewarm job queued: prewarm-job/na1-ephemeral-202603 started.
infra-bot: Observability: disk IO on those GPUs also spiked; eviction might be triggered by transient memory pressure on runtime. Suggest draining nodes with >85% GPU mem alloc.
jason: rolling drain for 3 most-affected nodes scheduled, starting now.
liam: rollback canary passed on 3 nodes. Rollback to previous runtime config looks good for canary. Shall we promote?
anika: promote to 50% traffic in na1.
ops-bot: Deploy promoted: runtime-service canary -> 50% (na1).
ryan: after promotion and drains, 99p at 430ms, miss rate down to 6%.
maya: keep traffic shifting policy in place for 30m and continue auto-evac monitoring.
jason: cost note — shifting 20% to eu-west will increase cross-region egress billing; tracking in incident ticket.
liam: opened infra-incident#624 with timeline, actions, and cost estimate.
anika: will follow-up with postmortem once stable. Big thanks to everyone for quick triage. :clap:
ops-bot: Incident annotation added to timeline: rollback performed, batch cap applied, nodes drained, traffic shifted.
infra-bot: Automated alert suppression for this signature enabled for 10m to avoid noise.
ryan: marking this thread as monitored — alerting if 99p > 700ms for next 30m.
maya: current status: latency stabilizing. Closing active mitigations in 20m if no regressions.
jason: FYI we should add an integration test to catch eviction spikes from combined batch+eviction heuristic changes.
anika: noted. Will put on eng-infra backlog and assign owner.
ryan: thanks all, keep updates here if anything regresses.
